facts.t: GST required amending the Constitution itself
facts.d: The 101st Amendment inserted Article 246A, which lets both Parliament and state legislatures tax the same transaction — an exception carved into the very structure of the Seventh Schedule. Nothing else in Indian tax law works this way.

facts.t: Alcohol and petroleum were left outside on purpose
facts.d: They are the two largest sources of independent state revenue. Excluding them was the price of getting the states to agree to GST at all — which is why the promise of one nation, one tax has always carried an asterisk.

From 22 September 2025 the standard rate became 18%, with a separate 40% band for luxury and sin goods. Health and life insurance premiums moved to zero — one of the few times a GST reform removed a tax entirely rather than moving it between slabs.

bank.q: GST was implemented in India in:
With reference to the rate structure effective from 22 September 2025, consider the following statements:
s: 18% became the new standard rate, replacing 28% for most goods and services.
A 40% band applies to luxury and sin goods.
Health and life insurance premiums are exempt.
bank.e: All three are correct. Essentials remain at 5%, covering household goods, packed food, clothing, footwear and pharmaceuticals.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT outside the ambit of GST?
o: None of these — all three are outside GST
bank.e: Tobacco is inside GST, taxed at the highest 40% band. Alcohol and select petroleum products remain outside it.

bank.as: GST has been described as having centralising tendencies.
bank.rs: As a destination-based levy it shifts revenue away from manufacturing-heavy producing states.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. A production state now collects on what it consumes rather than what it makes, which is at the heart of the fiscal-autonomy objection.

bank.q: Consider the following advantages attributed to GST:
s: Elimination of cascading through input tax credit.
A self-policing structure that makes evasion harder.
Immediate simplification of compliance for small enterprises.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Technology and compliance burdens on SMEs with limited digital literacy are listed among the problems, not the gains.

bank.q: The GST compensation arrangement guaranteed states revenue growth of:
bank.e: 14% annual growth from a 2015-16 base, for the five years from 2017 to 2022. Delays in paying it became a major Centre–State flashpoint.

bank.q: All of the following are criticisms in the Public Accounts Committee's assessment EXCEPT:
o: Roughly a two-percentage-point drop in indirect tax revenue between FY18 and FY20
Frequent rate changes and multiple filings creating complexity
Delays in releasing compensation to states
Failure to create a common national market
bank.e: A common national market is consistently listed among GST's genuine achievements. The criticisms concern delivery, complexity and revenue performance.

bank.q: Which rate now applies to essentials such as packed food, clothing and pharmaceuticals?
bank.e: 5%. Zero applies to health and life insurance premiums after the 2025 revision.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about GST and federalism:
s: It required states to surrender significant independent taxing powers.
Compensation was designed as a transitional guarantee against revenue loss.
States retain full autonomy to set their own GST rates.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Rates are set collectively through the GST Council; no state can set its own.

bank.as: GST is said to have lowered logistics costs.
bank.rs: The removal of interstate check posts and entry taxes streamlined supply chains.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — one of the clearest measurable gains from the transition.
